question.problem:
$$
f(x,y)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{3}{10}(x{y}^{3}+2), & \,0\le 2x\le y\le 2 \\ 0, & \,\text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

The joint probability density function $f(x,y)$ for the continuous random variables $X$ and $Y$ is shown above. Given that 

$$
\text{E}[X]=\frac{3}{7},\,\text{E}[Y]=\frac{52}{35},\,\text{SD}[X]≈0.2575,\,\text{SD}[Y]≈0.4389,
$$

 
find the correlation coefficient of $X$ and $Y.$ Round your answer to $2$ decimal places.
question.worked_solution:
Recall that the correlation coefficient of the random variables $X$ and $Y$ is defined as

$$
\rho =\frac{\text{Cov}[X,Y]}{\text{SD}[X]\cdot \text{SD}[Y]},
$$

where

- $\text{Cov}[X,Y]$ is the covariance, and

- $\text{SD}[X]$ and $\text{SD}[Y]$ are the standard deviations of $X$ and $Y.$

First, by applying the rule of the lazy statistician, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[XY] & ={∬}_{{R}^{2}}xy\,f(x,y)\,\text{d}x\text{d}y \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{2x}^{2}xy\cdot \frac{3}{10}(x{y}^{3}+2)\,\text{d}y]\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3}{10}{\int }_{0}^{1}[{\int }_{2x}^{2}({x}^{2}{y}^{4}+2xy)\,\text{d}y]\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3}{10}{\int }_{0}^{1}{[\frac{1}{5}{x}^{2}{y}^{5}+x{y}^{2}]}_{y=2x}^{y=2}\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3}{10}{\int }_{0}^{1}(\frac{32}{5}{x}^{2}+4x-\frac{32}{5}{x}^{7}-4{x}^{3})\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{3}{10}{[\frac{32}{15}{x}^{3}+2{x}^{2}-\frac{4}{5}{x}^{8}-{x}^{4}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{3}{10}\cdot \frac{35}{15} \\  & =\frac{7}{10}.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we compute the covariance and get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Cov}[X,Y] & =\text{E}[XY]-\text{E}[X]\cdot \text{E}[Y] \\  & =\frac{7}{10}-(\frac{3}{7})(\frac{52}{35}) \\  & =\frac{31}{490}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the correlation coefficient is 

$$
\begin{aligned}\rho  & =\frac{\text{Cov}[X,Y]}{\text{SD}[X]\cdot \text{SD}[Y]} \\  & ≈\frac{(\frac{31}{490})}{(0.2575)\cdot (0.4389)} \\  & ≈0.56,\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $2$ decimal places.
